s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
key_facts: Hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia in March 2020
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS
Relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye
Mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema in the right eye
Normal complete blood cell counts and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and had a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2

shortlist.label: Viral optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed blurred vision and redness in one eye, with relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision

shortlist.label: Retinal vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluorescein Angiography showed fluorescein leakage from retinal venules inferotemporal to the macula

shortlist.label: Post-infectious optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had recent close contact with a fatal case and developed ocular symptoms after hospitalization for pneumonia

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema, which can be associated with sarcoidosis

raw.rationale: The patient's recent close contact with a fatal case, hospitalization for severe bilateral pneumonia, and positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 suggest a recent viral infection. The development of blurred vision, redness, and pain in one eye, along with relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision, are consistent with optic neuritis. The absence of other neurological symptoms and normal CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR results support a post-infectious rather than a direct viral cause.

rejected.label: COVID-19
rejected.why: While the patient is positive for SARS-CoV-2, the ocular symptoms are more specific for an inflammatory condition like optic neuritis rather than a direct effect of COVID-19.

rejected.label: Viral optic neuritis
rejected.why: This is a possible diagnosis, but the term is more general and does not specify the post-infectious nature as clearly as post-infectious optic neuritis.

rejected.label: Retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has some signs of retinal vasculitis, the primary issue appears to be optic neuritis, making this a less comprehensive explanation for the patient's condition.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels and lack of other systemic symptoms make sarcoidosis less likely.
